accuracy.evidence: Curriculum lines checked against Development Matters (DfE 2023) 3 and 4 year olds (use all their senses, explore how things work, explore and talk about forces they can feel, understand why questions) and Head Start ELOF goal P-SCI 4 with its 36 to 48 month indicator. Magnet facts: only iron, steel and a few other metals are attracted; aluminium foil is not, and food tins are tinplate steel. Rain soaking in, running off to rivers and evaporating are all real paths, and snails withdraw to avoid predators and drying out.

misconceptions.evidence: Targets the documented early-years beliefs: that asking why is silly or naughty (asking prediction, Mia and Tom items, silly and naughty feedback), that a guess must be right (guess prediction, refusal of the no idea card, sad and never feedback), and the classic science slip that shiny or metal things stick to magnets (foil prediction, foil test, shiny and metal feedback). Sorting before testing on the magnet is refused, which targets guessing instead of finding out.

lab_distinct.evidence: flagcurio follows the inquiry cycle for 3 and 4 year olds: wonder taps in a garden, an asking versus telling sort, open guesses where every real guess is welcomed but stopping is not, a magnet test bench with sticks and does-not-stick shelves that only fill after a test, and matching questions to look, try or ask. No other lab models guessing before finding out or a magnet test, and it passed the 30 percent shingle gate against flaghuh, flagwonder, flagask and every other lab.

lab_teaches.evidence: The child commits to an answer on foil before testing and sees it fall to the does-not-stick shelf beside the paper clip and food tin, so the iron and steel rule is discovered rather than told. Guess cards always lead to a find-out sentence, so the child experiences guess then find out, and the matching step shows that some questions (why is the sky blue) cannot be answered by looking or trying.

predictions.evidence: Three locked predictions, each with a tempting wrong option: asking why is silly versus good, a guess must be right versus a guess helps you start, and shiny foil will stick versus will not. The step outcomes answer each one (asking cards sorted as the scientist's tool, every guess welcomed, foil on the does-not-stick shelf) and the done message echoes the learner's prediction.

challenge_feedback.evidence: Six rotating challenge questions with twelve tagged wrong-answer messages (quiet, bore, silly, naughty, tell, like, shiny, metal, bath, give, sad, never). Each names the slip, for example shiny does not mean it sticks because foil did not stick in the lab, or I like fish tells how you feel and does not ask anything.

readability.evidence: Family audience gates pass: kid paragraphs score about FK grade minus 0.2 with words such as wonder, guess, look, try it; adult paragraphs are about FK 6.9 against the 10.0 limit and still use the precise terms scientific inquiry, prediction, evidence, Characteristics of Effective Learning and P-SCI 4. Canvas labels are one to six words for pre-readers, with emoji on every tile.

no_filler.evidence: Content gate passed with no filler phrases and explanation overlap under 12 percent against every lesson, including Exploring Ideas Through Talk, Asking Questions and Question Words. Each adult paragraph gives curriculum lines, research findings (Chouinard 2007, Frazier, Gelman and Wellman 2009), named mistakes or the lab's tasks.

mobile.evidence: Walkthrough passed on iPhone 13 and desktop. iPhone screenshots at 390 px in dark and light themes show the six garden tiles with emoji and names, the four guess tiles in a 2 by 2 grid, the magnet with two shelves, and three way-to-find-out boxes, all unclipped, with large young-mode buttons (56 px) below for every action.

accessibility.evidence: axe-core reports no WCAG 2.1 AA violations in light or dark theme. The canvas aria-label speaks each question, guess and test result, every drag or tap has a labelled button (for example Test the shiny foil on the magnet, or What is under this stone? Find out: Look), and canvas text uses theme ink on pale or slate tiles.
